narrative: OMX30 enters Tuesday underpinned by modest global risk appetite (Nikkei +1.74%, NASDAQ +0.82%) and a weaker oil complex (-4.78% Brent), but technical momentum remains anaemic with ADX at 6.5 signalling low directional conviction. The index sits above its 200-MA (+2.9%) but below the 50-MA (-0.7%), trapped in a consolidation zone typical of mean-reverting choppy trading. RSI at 52.26 and Stochastic neutral offer no extremes to trigger reversal trades, while MACD remains below signal line with negative histogram at -3.971. The dollar firmness (USD/SEK +0.27%, DXY +0.23%) and copper bounce (+1.47%) are modest tailwinds for export-heavy industrials and Boliden, but the macro backdrop—particularly UK budget risks and geopolitical noise—argues for defensive positioning ahead of US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET.
morningBrief: OMX30 likely opens flatly to +0.2% as European correlation bleeds through but ADX weakness caps upside enthusiasm. Industrials (Atlas Copco, Volvo B) benefit from USD/SEK tailwind and lower oil, but sector conviction is muted with ADX in neutral-to-weak regime—watch the 3180 level (50-MA) as intraday resistance; support at 3085 (lower Bollinger band). Banks trade mixed: yield curve flat (US 10Y at 4.986%, essentially unchanged) limits NIM expansion, so SEB A and Handelsbanken A unlikely to accelerate. Boliden is the outlier—copper +1.47% and gold firm provide direct revenue lift; initiate longs on any dip. H&M B faces dual headwind from weak EUR/SEK and persistent China weakness (Shanghai -1.33%). Pharma (AstraZeneca, Essity) stable but not flight-to-quality rotation yet (VIX compression, no panic). Watch for any catalysts from US jobless claims (14:30 CET) and further China data deterioration; if risk-off accelerates, rotate defensives and trim export exposure. Key risk: trade escalation could flip sentiment fast—keep tight stops.
